lines.text: Did you know... that one of the most famous goals in history should never have counted? And the only man who could stop it... never saw it.
For a hundred years, football had a secret. The referee's eyes were the only truth. And eyes... can be fooled.
Welcome to a WorldCup twenty-six Bonus. Did you know?
The injustices. The rules that rewrote the game. A tribute that breaks your heart. And a future you are not ready for.
Five secrets of the World Cup. Most fans know none of them. Stay with me.
It begins with the age before the machines.
Did you know... in nineteen eighty-six, Diego Maradona scored against England... with his hand?
He punched the ball into the net. The referee never saw it. The goal stood. Argentina won, two-one.
He called it the Hand of God. Today, it would be erased in seconds. Back then, there was nothing.
And in twenty ten, England's Frank Lampard struck the ball against Germany. It crossed the line by a foot.
No goal was given. There was no technology to see it. England went home. The world demanded change.
Did you know... a single rule once reinvented football overnight?
After a slow, dull nineteen ninety, they made one change. Goalkeepers could no longer pick up a pass from their own team.
The back-pass rule, nineteen ninety-two. Suddenly the game had to be played at speed. Football was never slow again.
Then, the machines arrived.
Did you know... goal-line technology only came in twenty fourteen? A camera that knows, to the millimetre, when a ball has crossed.
Four years later, the biggest change of all. Twenty eighteen. The first World Cup with V-A-R.
The very first review handed France a penalty. And the number of penalties... almost doubled overnight.
And in twenty twenty-two, it went further. Did you know the ball itself became a sensor?
Inside it, a chip sending its position five hundred times a second. Twelve cameras tracking every limb. The offside... judged by machine.
But not every secret is about technology. Some are about the heart.
Did you know... Portugal walk out for this World Cup carrying an extra name?
On every player's wrist, a bracelet. It reads: tribute to Jota.
Diogo Jota, the forward they lost in twenty twenty-five. The teammate who never left the team. They play, now, for him.
Which leaves one question. If the machines can already see everything... what comes next?
Here is what we predict. Within ten years, the referee's whistle may be the last human decision left.
An AI that judges offside, handball, and fouls in an instant. A ball that calls its own goals. Mistakes... erased forever.
The game your grandchildren watch may never know a wrong decision. For better... or for worse.
So — how many did you know? Comment the number, one to five.
And play the future yourself. At WorldCup twenty-six dot world, pick three of the forty-eight nations — every goal they score, scores for you.
Free to play, no prizes. Like, share, subscribe — and keep asking... did you know?
